title: Marc Jacobs Daisy vs Marc Jacobs Daisy Love
summary: Marc Jacobs Daisy is the crisp original floral, and Daisy Love is the sweeter, gourmand-leaning update. Compare notes and longevity before choosing.
body_markdown:
Marc Jacobs Daisy launched the franchise in 2007. Marc Jacobs Daisy Love arrived more than a decade later with a noticeably sweeter, gourmand-leaning take on the same idea.[Marc Jacobs Daisy](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/marc-jacobs-daisy-1029941) and[Marc Jacobs Daisy Love](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/marc-jacobs-daisy-love-1577) share a name and a design language, but the notes inside tell two different stories.


Marc Jacobs Daisy, the original 2007 floral


## What Daisy and Daisy Love Share


Both fragrances build around a central floral idea layered over fruit, and both were composed by Alberto Morillas with the same easy, low-effort wear in mind. Neither demands much thought to apply, and both hold up across most seasons rather than being tied to a single one. The bottle design carries the same daisy-topped cap across both, a visual thread that ties the newer release back to the original even though the fragrances inside diverge fairly quickly.


## Marc Jacobs Daisy: The Crisp Original


Marc Jacobs Daisy starts crisp, with violet leaf and grapefruit cutting through the air before strawberry and jasmine round the edges into something softer. The heart settles into gardenia alongside that jasmine and violet, and the base brings in white musk, woody notes, and vanilla for warmth without heaviness. On skin, Daisy typically lasts 6 to 8 hours, with soft to moderate projection that pulls in close after the first hour. Its structure stays floral throughout, never tipping into anything that reads as dessert.


## Marc Jacobs Daisy Love: The Gourmand Update


Daisy Love opens with cloudberry, a tart, slightly sweet fruit note that sets a different tone from the original’s grapefruit and strawberry pairing. The heart is built around a daisy tree floral accord rather than the violet, gardenia, and jasmine trio in the original, giving it a rounder, more singular floral impression. The base brings in driftwood and cashmere musk, a combination that reads warmer and sweeter than Daisy’s woody musk and vanilla. Composed by Alberto Morillas, the same perfumer behind the original, Daisy Love leans further into the gourmand direction, with a softness that borders on comforting rather than crisp. Longevity tends to run 6 to 8 hours, similar to the original, but the cashmere musk base gives it slightly more warmth on skin as the day goes on. Skip it if the sharper violet-leaf opening of the original is the appeal, since Daisy Love, also available on Scentbird, trades that crispness for sweetness from the first spray.


## Daisy vs Daisy Love at a Glance


Marc Jacobs Daisy Daisy Love


Feel Crisp floral with a fruity top Sweet, gourmand-leaning floral


Main notes Violet leaf, gardenia, vanilla Cloudberry, daisy tree, cashmere musk


Lasts 6 to 8 hours 6 to 8 hours


Best for Fans of classic, crisp florals Fans of sweeter, warmer scents


## Which One Should You Choose?


The clearest differentiator is sweetness. The original Daisy keeps its floral core crisp and slightly powdery, while Daisy Love pushes the same basic idea toward something warmer and more dessert-adjacent. Both last a similar amount of time, so the decision really comes down to whether a sharper, classic floral or a rounder, sweeter one suits the way a person wants to smell day to day.


The verdict


Choose Marc Jacobs Daisy for the crisper, more classic floral with a powdery finish. Choose Marc Jacobs Daisy Love for a sweeter, gourmand-leaning update with a rounder floral heart. Longevity is close between the two, so personal taste in sweetness should drive the decision.


Description alone will not settle it, since the sweetness of Daisy Love reads differently on everyone. Give it real time on your skin before deciding either way.

## Frequently Asked Questions


What is the difference between Marc Jacobs Daisy and Daisy Love?


Daisy is the original 2007 floral built on violet leaf, gardenia, and vanilla, giving it a crisper, more classic profile. Daisy Love, from 2018, is built around cloudberry, a daisy tree floral accord, and cashmere musk, giving it a sweeter, gourmand-leaning finish.


Is Daisy Love sweeter than the original Daisy?


Yes, Daisy Love leans sweeter from the first spray thanks to cloudberry and cashmere musk. The original Daisy has vanilla in its base too, but its violet leaf and grapefruit opening keeps it crisper overall.


Which came first, Daisy or Daisy Love?


The original Marc Jacobs Daisy launched in 2007. Daisy Love followed more than a decade later, in 2018, as a warmer, sweeter take on the same idea.


Do Daisy and Daisy Love smell similar?


They share a floral core and the same overall easy-to-wear intent, but the specific notes differ quite a bit. Daisy leans on violet and gardenia, while Daisy Love centers on a daisy tree accord and driftwood, giving each a distinct personality.


Which lasts longer, Daisy or Daisy Love?


The two are fairly close, both typically running 6 to 8 hours on skin. Daisy Love’s cashmere musk base can give it slightly more warmth later in the day, though the difference is subtle rather than dramatic.


Which one is easier to wear daily, Daisy or Daisy Love?


Daisy is generally the easier daily option because of its crisper, less sweet profile, which suits a wider range of settings. Daisy Love works well daily too, but its sweetness may suit certain moods and seasons more than others.
